corrections.text: The article attributes the statement that combining the new approach with error correction "is the natural next step" toward making non-Abelian anyons "a practical foundation for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers" to Henrik Dreyer. The cited source, The Quantum Insider, attributes this material to Ruben Verresen (it follows a Verresen quote and is introduced with "he added"), and presents it as reported/indirect speech rather than a direct quotation. The underlying point is accurate; only the speaker attribution and quotation format were wrong.

The article cites both Quantum Computing Report and SDxCentral for the statistic that magic state distillation can consume "up to 90% of a machine's physical qubit and control resources." This figure is verbatim from Quantum Computing Report, but SDxCentral's article does not contain this statistic or any equivalent percentage; it only describes distillation generally as "one of the most resource-intensive techniques." The 90% figure should be attributed to Quantum Computing Report alone.
